reason: E1 shows Al2O3 addition in a different HEA system (CrFeCuMnNi) refines grains and increases compressive strength by 21%, supporting the grain refinement and strength premise. E2 shows 0.25 wt% Y2O3 in CrMnFeCoNi HEA increases strength by 15.2% via similar mechanisms, supporting the specific wt% and mechanism premises. However, neither study involves the caloric MM'X alloy system, nor do they demonstrate preservation of a magneto-structural transition or caloric response, leaving the premise of preserving functional properties unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Oxide nanoparticles (Al2O3) can be dispersed in a HEA matrix via mechanical alloying and sintering to refine grains and improve strength.
A small addition (~0.25 wt%) of oxide nanoparticles can increase compressive strength by ~15–20% in a HEA matrix.
The strengthening mechanism involves grain boundary pinning (Zener pinning), Orowan looping, and load transfer.
The oxide dispersion and strengthening can be achieved without fundamentally altering the matrix phase responsible for functional properties.
